key_insight: HullFT makes test-time finetuning faster and better by selecting a sparse, diverse support set with convex geometry, then reusing gradients across repeated examples.
engineering_relevance: The method targets a practical deployment bottleneck in per-query LLM adaptation, improving the quality–runtime tradeoff for retrieval-and-finetune pipelines.
method: Use Frank-Wolfe to approximate the query as a sparse convex combination of training sequence embeddings.
Integerize the fractional weights into a multiset for finetuning, creating repeated examples.
Apply Gradient Reuse to amortize forward-backward cost across those repetitions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower bits-per-byte at substantially lower total runtime than current state-of-the-art TTFT methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on efficient nearest-neighbor retrieval, stable convex optimization, and correct handling of repeated-example gradient caching at inference time.
paper_title: Efficient Test-Time Finetuning of LLMs via Convex Reconstruction and Gradient Caching
